work.permit: Licence from the Minister under section 3(2) of the Protection of Young Persons (Employment) Act 1996

note: Majority: the Age of Majority Act 1985 (No. 2 of 1985), section 2, gives full age at eighteen, or earlier on marriage; emancipation by marriage isn't held. Work: the Protection of Young Persons (Employment) Act 1996 (No. 16 of 1996) defines a child as a person under 16 or the school-leaving age, whichever is higher, and section 3(1) bars employing a child; the form holds 16. Section 3(4) lets a child over 14 do light work outside term (7 hours a day, 35 a week), and section 3(5) and (6) allow work experience; those aren't held. A child may perform in cultural, artistic, sports or advertising activities only under a licence the Minister grants in individual cases (section 3(2)); section 3(3) lets the Minister authorise over-13s by regulation. No age below which no licence is given is set, so no permitFrom. Hours limits for young persons (sections 5 and 6) aren't held. Service: the Defence Act 1954 (No. 18 of 1954), section 53, provides that a person may be enlisted in the Permanent Defence Force, on an attestation declaring his willingness; the Defence Forces' own magazine, An Cosantóir (May/June 2024), states that Ireland has never engaged in conscription and that volunteerism will remain a cornerstone of the Army; so service is none. Section 54 of the 1954 Act (enlistment for service during an emergency the Oireachtas declares) isn't held. Read from the Irish Statute Book's enacted texts on 2026-10-31; later amendments to the 1996 Act weren't checked against a revised text.

sources.title: Irish Statute Book: Age of Majority Act 1985 (No. 2 of 1985)
sources.said: Reduction of age of majority. 2. —(1) ... after such commencement when he attains the age of eighteen years or, in case he marries before attaining that age, upon his marriage

sources.title: Irish Statute Book: Protection of Young Persons (Employment) Act 1996 (No. 16 of 1996)
sources.said: “child” means a person who is under 16 years of age or the school-leaving age, whichever is the higher ... an employer shall not employ a child to do work. (2) The Minister may, by licence, authorise in individual cases, the employment of a child in cultural, artistic, sports or advertising activities

sources.title: Irish Statute Book: Defence Act 1954 (No. 18 of 1954)
sources.said: A person (including a minor) may be enlisted as a man of the Permanent Defence Force ... of his willingness to fulfil the engagements set out in the said attestation paper

sources.title: An Cosantóir (the Defence Forces magazine), May/June 2024
sources.said: Ireland has never engaged in conscription. Volunteerism has always and will remain a key corner stone of the Irish Army
